title: BIAN Payment Order service domain
body: Encapsulates initiation and lifecycle of a payment order. Target state for legacy payment-processing modules. Favours event-driven choreography over synchronous orchestration to reduce coupling and improve resilience under peak load.

title: BIAN Customer Offer service domain
body: Manages product offers presented to a customer. Suitable target for legacy product-catalogue and eligibility components currently embedded in monolithic onboarding flows.

title: Strangler Fig migration pattern
body: Incrementally route traffic from a legacy monolith to new services behind a facade, retiring legacy paths only once the replacement is proven. Reduces big-bang migration risk. Recommended sequencing when blast radius is high.

title: Shared database anti-pattern
body: Multiple services reading and writing the same database tables create hidden coupling, block independent deployment, and make data ownership ambiguous. Must be decomposed before service extraction. High migration-risk indicator.

title: Synchronous coupling anti-pattern
body: Long synchronous call chains across components propagate latency and failure. Convert to asynchronous, event-driven integration to bound blast radius and improve P99 latency.

title: Event-driven integration pattern
body: Components communicate via events on a durable broker rather than direct synchronous calls. Improves resilience, scalability, and independent deployability. Preferred target integration style for high-throughput BFSI platforms.
